page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Margin notes stand in the right margin. Footnotes in smaller type run below the text, at the foot of the page. Printed page number at top right, running head at top centre, gathering mark at bottom right.

main_text.p: & ineptias Rainoldi cuiusdam Ministri[?] Calviniani, quo cum Dei hominem de rebus controversiis conferre voluistis. Ineptiarum & fraudum argui potest quivis. Nihil tam volucre, quàm maledi-ctum, inquit {a}Pro PlacioCicero: nihil facilius emittitur.
Quòd si potuissent ullius fraudis aut ineptiæ Col-loquium Rainoldi cum Harto habitum convince-re: fecissent tot annorum spatio, ut credibile est.

Sed ille, qui appellat Hartum Dei hominem, cuius confessione nos legitimi tantum Principis primatum Reginæ tribuimus, ac non Pontificis summi: convincit suos esse homines {b}Ioh.8.44.diaboli, qui ob primatum summi Pontificis Principi denegatum Papistas laesæ Maiestatis damnatos mentiuntur; & à ministris hæreticis ad deferendam fidem Catholicam impulsos, quum ab orthodoxis ad exuendum hæreticum furorem urgerentur.Iam doctores nostros vobis odiosos reddere conantur, utinam mendaciis tantum levioribus, quibus nos traducunt, quando me, exempli gratia, Calvinianum; alios {c}Concert. Eccles. Cath. in Angl. adverf. Calvinop. & Purit.Puritanos, aut Calvinopapistas; & omnes, {d}Baron. annalib. eccles. passim.Novatores nominant. Etenim mediocris rerum in autoribus cuivis obviis animadversio sta-tim suggestura sit, nec ab hoc novandi crimine per stringi magis nos, quâ {e}A&.17.19.Paulu, cuius doctrina nova nuncupata est: nec ab illis conviciis Calvinianorum, Puritanorum, Calvinopapistarum, & quicquid simile fingent, turpiorem hodie aspergi orthodoxis maculam, quàm olim, quum ab iniquis {f}A&. 24.5.Nazare-ni, {g}Clem. Alex. Strom. lib.4. Tertull. de ieiunio adversus Psychicos.Psychici, {h}Vi&. Vric.[?] de perfe-quut. VVad.Homousiani, {i}Eustathiani, {k}Macariani, {l}Pagani vocabantur. page.notes: Printed "B 3" at the foot is the gathering mark. A decorative capital precedes "Ministri"; I could not read it, so the word is marked [?]. The marginal note "Vi&. Vric." is doubtful. The word "Paulu" is copied as printed and may be read "Pauli". Underlining in the text (under "doctores nostros", "Iam", "nuncupata", "Nazare-ni") is ink, not transcribed. Show-through and the page edge are left out. The paragraph continues onto the next page after "di-". Printed s is rendered as plain s throughout; printed f in "Homoufiani", "Euftathiani", "Papiftas" and "Calvinopapiftas" is long s and is copied as s.
